utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances for today, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Joanna Korner assisted by Crispian Smith, Case Manager, for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Dragan Krgovic and Miroslav Cuskic for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. Would the Usher please -- sorry. Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just mention before the witness is brought in, the question of an exercise, which, unfortunately is going take a little time. And can I explain to Your Honours what I -- spent some time myself yesterday looking at. Your Honours will recall that there were some questions that I put to Mr. Tutus about the reports that he had put in against the special police members. Then the document in 1993, the letter, which in fact encapsulates most, if not all, of those reports, and a list of the payroll for special police in August, plus a full list obviously compiled later but attached to the same document of the special police. Now, although Mr. Tutus had during the course of looking at the documents actually identified two people who he said were still there when he put in criminal reports, he didn't do that in court. And at that stage I hadn't gone through the exercise which I did yesterday. Mr. Krgovic equally objected to what I was saying. So I have done the exercise. Your Honour, can I put it this way, and I can demonstrate this to Your Honours and with the witness. With -- with one exception, the -- the names against whom he put in complaints of criminal conduct in June and July of 1992, appear on the payroll for August 1992, and in the list of the full list of the special police, or -- whether it is full or not, but it's a later list, those names appear again with what actually seems to have happened to them. In respect of the incident that -- as it were, seems to have prompted this long report in 1993, which took place in this -- in -- I've forgotten the name of the place it is. Karanovac. None of the -- the earlier people appear except as members in the community and not actually specifically alleged to have committed the offence, but they appear as members of the special -- ex-special Banja Luka special police who live in the community where the complaints have come. Now, Your Honour, can I do that all with the witness but it means going through a number of documents. And that will take clearly more time than have I left. But -- obviously, I leave this in the hands of Your Honours. I can do this exercise using a couple of examples or I can do it in full, or I cannot do with the witness at all and simply show Your Honours. So that's why I'm raising it at this stage before I begin my -- my further examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If I may ask -- before we rule, if I may -- to aid my own understanding. We're talking about documents, the contents of which speak for themselves.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And what we're looking at is a method of isolating from these documents that overlap the period of the indictment such of the -- in terms of names particularly, as are specific -- well, as are relevant for our purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The exercise -- the whole point of this line of questioning and the exercise I'd done, Your Honour, is to demonstrate if necessary to the witness, although we would say that he clearly knows about that, however reluctant he is, that despite in some cases actual criminal reports and in other cases we don't have criminal reports but Official Notes, all of which are listed in his 1993 report, it would appear, on the face of the documents, that no action was taken to remove these people from the special police. Certainly not by August. And if one looks at the document which is attached to it, one can see, which is obviously a later document, 1993, that most of these people, as I say, with one exception which is an interesting -- went on working in the special police and went on to other jobs when it was disbanded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: All the documents to which you have referred, Ms. Korner, have been admitted into evidence; is that correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: They have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Yes. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: If I may say something. [Interpretation] Your Honours, in my cross-examination I will deal precisely with these matters raised by the Prosecutor, so if the document is self-explanatory, as far as the Defence position is concerned, I do not mind if the Prosecutor wants to go through the document with the witness, using a few examples. But, of course, I will deal with it in cross-examination, of course, trying to prove the opposite.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, it seems to us that if you simply proceed in the ordinary manner, to elicit the foundation of evidence from the witness, then we should be -- the matter should resolve itself. We'll see how it goes. Because the -- what Mr. Krgovic has indicated seems to be a helpful and practical method of solving the problem. But the exercise is to get the evidence on the record from the witness who is on the stand to explain the -- what happened in respect of these persons against whom complaints were made.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Before you answer. We are of the view that can you use just a few examples.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: And then put the question to him of how he interprets the fact that they were still in service in August, and that's what we need.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, well, that's helpful. I will pick a couple of examples, then, and deal with it. Your Honours, I -- I'm sorry. Because it is a -- because of having to have the documents up, although we copied them in hard copy for him so can he deal with it quicker, and I have three -- three more documents which I need to put to this witness. It's going to take longer than, I think, the ten minutes or so I have left. That's all I'm asking, at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, let's start.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Good morning to you, Mr. Tutus. Before Ms. Korner resumes her examination-in-chief, I remind you you're still on your oath.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I want you, please, to have a look at a document which is -- it's already an exhibit, P685. This is an document dated the 9th of October, 1992, addressed to all SJBs. It's a dispatch again, and it's got Stojan Zupljanin's signature, passing on a memorandum from the Main Staff of the Army of the Republika Srpska saying that: "The Presidency has no information on crimes committed against the Serbian people in the zone of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps ..." Do you remember getting this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I did, but I can't remember it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And all I want to ask you about is this: The zone of responsibility of the 1st Krajina Corps, was that, although not entirely completely, the area that covered Banja Luka and other municipalities, such as Sanski Most, Kotor Varos, and the like?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so. I don't know if that's the entire area; but, generally speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, I agree. I mean, that there's more. Thank you very much. That's all I want to ask you about that document. Could you look now, please, at document 65 ter 75. I'm sorry, it's going back to April.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we just look at the -- the -- it's the third page, because of the way it's been copied, for some reason, in B/C/S, and the second page in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, is this a report sent both to the CSB and the Ministry of the Interior signed by your chief of the crime section, Zoran Josic?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't need to ask you anything more about the contents. I just need to --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1093, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Next could you look, please, at a document marked 664, 65 ter 664.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we need to look at the second page -- well, let's stick to the first page for the moment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is a dispatch of the 18th of September addressed to SJBs, to the MUP for information, and to the 1st and 2nd Krajina Corps, and to leaders of all organisationals -- of organisational units. Can you go -- can we go to the second page, please, in each. Yeah, and we can see again that it goes under the name of Stojan Zupljanin. Then -- I think this is -- stay on the second page in B/C/S and I think it's the last paragraph, but need to go back to the first page in English, the last paragraph on -- in the English page. And I think it's the last paragraph also in the B/C/S. It says: "... we draw the attention of SJB chiefs" -- "to the attention of SJB chiefs the fact that members of the active and reserve police forces may be engaged in combat activities according to the principle of resubordination to a superior army command only in the event that combat activities are taking place on the territory covered by the designated SJBs and with the approval of the chief ..." This document was in September, Mr. Tutus. Do you know why Mr. Zupljanin was reminding SJB chiefs of this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But it is a document you would have got?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I certainly did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honours, may that be admitted and marked, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P1094, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And could you now go, please, to a document which is already exhibited, P782.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is that a document signed by you with a stamp on it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is dated the 24th of November. And it says: "The following confiscated weapons are stored at this SJB," and you then give a list. Is that a list of all the weapons you confiscated and kept from April 1992 or only from November?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would first have to see the dispatch sent by the centre, the reference number indicated here, and these are only weapons confiscated under -- on the grounds indicated in items 1, 2, and 3. Administrative proceedings and criminal proceedings. If a crime is involved, the weapon is confiscated as evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All I'm asking what is the administrative procedure? That's what you described that you were doing for disarmament, is it? You remember we discussed the day before yesterday the disarming of the population in compliance with the directive issued by the Autonomous Region of Krajina, Assembly or Crisis Staff, and I'm -- just want to know whether administrative procedure refers to that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm not sure that's what it means. There were some weapons confiscated without any proceedings going on, so I don't know if such weapons are included in any of the three categories. I don't think they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If you were confiscating illegal weapons during this period, would you launch a criminal proceedings against the person in possession? In other words, put in a criminal report.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were elements of criminal liability we would certainly file a criminal report. However, if it concerned a member of the VRS who legally owned a weapon, as a member of the unit, and then illegally left the unit together with a weapon, and then the army put out a bulletin, because he was a deserter and thus illegally owned a weapon, or failed to respond to mobilisation, then he was liable under the Law on Territorial Defence, we would confiscated such a weapon. But that was the responsibility of military organs, and in such cases, we did not start any proceedings or file reports.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but -- I'm asking at the moment about the procedure you described whereby you were searching people's houses for illegal weapons. And leave aside for the moment lawfully owned hunting rifles. If you confiscated what you thought were illegal weapons, would you put in a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I want to say the following. We didn't go from house to house at random and search them. We sought weapons on the basis of indicia, evidence. You couldn't just enter someone's house if there was no evidence that there were weapons illegally held there. And secondly, I tried to explain that when you seize military weapons, well, I wasn't referring to weapons owned by citizens legally. It concerned military weapons legally given to them previously, but the security organs illegally had them because they didn't respond to the mobilisation call-up. I don't know if this answer is satisfactory or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Can I ask the question again. You told us the day before yesterday that you carried out, on the basis of information, searches of people's houses to see whether they possessed illegal weapons. That is to say, no permit and a weapon that they had unlawfully. Would you then file a criminal report against the person who was in such possession? Very simple question.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it was a military weapon, then the military organs were responsible.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, but even if it was a military weapon, you still had to file a report, didn't you, and it was then a question for the prosecutor to decide whether it went to the military court or stayed in the civil court. Now, please, answer the question: Did you file criminal reports against persons in possession of illegal weapons.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we did. But in some cases, the army did that too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm talking about cases -- make this quite clear. I'm talking about cases where members of your police conducted a search and discovered that they -- what they believed to be an illegal weapon in possession of a civilian, or someone who wasn't in the military, or the police. Would you then file a criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most frequently, yes. I don't see why we wouldn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You may not see -- all right. I think --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, did you or did you not file reports in such events?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In principle, we did. But I cannot now claim that in some cases that were the responsibility of the military security organs and the military and judiciary, I can't say that we didn't refer the case to them, and as a result, we didn't file a criminal report. That's what I'm saying. In cases where we believed that it was our responsibility to file a criminal report, we did so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. It wasn't your decision, was it, as a police officer, to which court a case went? You filed a criminal report and it was the decision of the prosecutor, was it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The crime police did this. They would assess whether something was the responsibility of the military organs or the civil organs. But there were cases in which we had a report from the civilian prosecutor and he would then refer it to the military prosecutor. Or, rather, we would refer a case to the civilian prosecutor and the civilian prosecutor would then refer it to the military prosecutor. There were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now, and can we just make -- can you just confirm whether this is correct, that the Official Notes that we looked at about the activities of the special police are not the same as criminal reports?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In respect of some of the reports we looked at, and, in particular, perhaps we can look at the one -- the first of these reports against the special police.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Could we have a look, please, at ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, you say "report." Is it criminal report you mean or is it Official Note?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: A difference between -- did I not say "criminal report"? I thought I did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: You say "report."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, I -- sorry, no. Now I'm getting my -- yes, a document. It's not a report. It's not a criminal report, this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: It's an Official Note.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's the one, in fact, that Judge Harhoff remarked on yesterday and I ... okay, it's tab 19. Tab 19. What number is that? P1081. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: While that is being sought, put up on the screen, Mr. Tutus, did you have daily meetings with the chief of the crime police?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was obligatory, and we also had meetings with the police station commander almost on a daily basis, together with this person.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Right. And wouldn't he then fill you in about arrests that had been made for illegal possession of weapons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He would fill us in with regard to more serious matters.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Now we've got this document up again on the screen. 4th of June, which on the first we looked at, which is not -- this is not a criminal report, is it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document in front of me. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has to do with a dispatch in which we informed the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and CSB about certain events.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. What I want to know is, why, on the 4th of June, and we've seen it with other such documents, you're sending it not only to the CSB chief but also to the Ministry of the Interior? Because this is not a result -- you don't refer to any requests from the minister of the -- Ministry of the Interior. This is your decision to send it also to the -- the -- the Ministry of Interior. Why was that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I thought that it was a serious case and that it was necessary for the Ministry of the Interior to be informed of it. That's probably the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because you only had the duty, didn't you, to report to the head of the -- the chief of the CSB?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. Leading.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'll rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To whom was it your duty to report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To the CSB and the MUP of the Republic of Serbia [as interpreted], in accordance with the instructions that had been issued.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And which instructions are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: On mutual information, the instructions on mutual information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That document was in force before the war in the former Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It was signed by the former Secretariat for Internal Affairs, and the document is called Instructions on Mutual, Current and Temporary Information, or instruction. It told us when we had to inform the MUP and the CSB about certain events.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Just a correction for the transcript. Page 13, line 14 -- line 6 and 7, the Republika Srpska is concerned, not the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Before I do what I'm afraid is going to be a rather boring exercise, can I just ask you finally this on -- on Banja Luka. During the course of 1992, whether a number of international organisations which were either visiting in or had a base in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they had their base in Banja Luka and they would go to Banja Luka, to visit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The -- what was then called the European Community Monitoring Mission, was that in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If those are the people in white uniforms, then I believe that, yes, they did visit. I think those are the people concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. The UN High Commission for Refugees was that also -- did that also have a base and people from that organisation visiting Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember a visit by Mrs. Rehn, Ole [sic] Rehn, I think that's the name. She would visit. She saw President Radic, and I was present too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In addition to that, did you receive a number of visits from international journalists?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have the opportunity of speaking to international journalists. I don't remember that. But there were frequent meetings with President Radic. Foreign representatives would have meetings with him, but as to whether there were journalists among them, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we now finally and please do this rather boring exercise, or a few examples. Yesterday, day before yesterday, we looked at your -- sometimes criminal reports, sometimes information reports about the behaviour of members of the special police unit, largely in June and July. Now, I'm going give you, because I think it may be easier for you although we will bring it up on the screen as well, copies of, first of all, the document which was your information in 1993, which is Exhibit P628, and also a copy of the list, the payroll for August 1992 for the special police and a further, obviously later list which appears to the full list of -- of the special police, which is document 1092. Can you have them in -- we'll give them to you so it is easier for you to follow this. But we will have to have it up on the screen for the rest.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What we have done, Your Honours, and hopefully this will make it easier, in Sanction we've got both documents up. I don't know how people -- oh, I see -- yes, in English. We obviously can't do this exercise side by side in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we -- you start off this information, if you go to the second page there, and if we go to the second page on -- yeah, thank you very much, with this complaint that has come in 1993 from the Karanovac community. And then you explain that you have had negative experiences with members of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre special purposes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Now can we go, then, please, in the English to page 3 of that document. And in the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: The accused cannot follow the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, there's no way of doing this, as I say -- I'm sure that you have got hard copies in -- in -- in -- with you and if they can be given to the accused. We can't -- there's no way of doing this so that everybody can follow with four separate documents on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just in principle, it's -- this -- these accused are on trial, so ... at least they should be able to -- to follow the evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The only thing that is going to be followed is the names and the names are the same in English. So I hope that they can just look at the screen and see the names.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the problem is that these lists have certain comments on them. There are certain notes made on these lists and that is what is important in this particular case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you. We're advised that the documents may be printed out in B/C/S for the benefit of the accused within a couple of minutes. So while that's being done, I suppose Ms. Korner can continue, and the accused will catch up. Mr. Krgovic, Mr. Zecevic, that shouldn't be a problem, should it?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, and I appreciate the help of the Registry as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: In paragraph 3 of this 1993 report there is a complaint relating to the 2nd of June, 1992, of a beating and the man in question is said to be Mr. Kajkut, who presumably is a relation of the Kajkut we talked about -- well, he may not be. The name's obviously quite similar, but anyhow. Member of the Banja Luka special police services detachment. If you look then at number 10 on the payroll for August 1992, there is Mr. Kajkut. Although it appears his money was collected by somebody else with the same name.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the original B/C/S, there are signatures by each of these ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on the basis of the name and surname, it could be the same person. But to identify him we need the other details. The date of birth, father's name, and so on and so forth. Everything is possible, you know. Perhaps there are several individuals with the same name, but this seems to show that the same person is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Did you put in a criminal report about this incident? Because you don't refer to it in this summary; whereas, we'll see later you do refer to criminal reports in other cases.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember individual reports. I don't know how this ended. We probably did. There was no reason not to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, because -- would you describe this as a serious incident, beating somebody?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's unlawful behaviour. As to how serious it is, well, there were more serious incidents.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if we ... if you go on in that second document, please, to the list of the special police detachment, the alphabetical one, you go to number 116, you'll see there that he's a candidate for some course.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yeah. Now, you make no reference to either any criminal proceedings that were taken against him or, indeed, disciplinary proceedings. Would you have expected, first, that criminal proceedings would have been taken in this case?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Given what it says under -- are you referring to what it says under item 3, information?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am. I am.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I think criminal proceedings should have been instituted if there was sufficient information, and this seems to show there was sufficient information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: What about disciplinary, if nothing else?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Would you retain as a member of your police force, in the SJB, a person who had committed this kind of crime?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say he committed a crime. I would have checked everything and tried to establish the truth on the basis of the relevant procedure.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes -- no, if it was shown whether, for the purposes of -- of -- of criminal prosecution or disciplinary, that this man had done what is said he did there, would have you kept him in your police force?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it had been confirmed that this was correct, I wouldn't [Realtime transcript read in error "would"] have kept him. But as far as I know, he never completed a course of any kind.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: How do you know? Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, then, was there a criminal proceedings against him?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly now. But I think so.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The work --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm so sorry to interrupt 19, 12, 13, page 19, line 12 and 13. I believe the witness said, "I would not have -- I would not have kept him." And it's recorded as he would have kept him. I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. I don't want to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's fine. Thank you very much, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: But he still stayed in the special police?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: Objection. Leading. It does not appear from the list.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, in August of 1992 he is on the payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the documents -- and the Prosecution knows that the unit was disbanded on the 10th of August, and that an agreement was reached. The witness will appear who will talk about this. It was agreed that all members should receive their salaries for August although they weren't in fact members of the special police in August. That is the point of my objection. The Prosecution is aware of that fact because there's a series of documents that demonstrate this. So this is the reason for my objection. The witness is being led.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Up until, and I accept entirely that the order disbanding them came in the 10th of August, up until the 10th of August, if this payroll is accurate, accept all that, it shows that this gentleman was still in the special police for the rest of June, presumably, July, and August. Doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are you asking me that question?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRGOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution refrain from asking leading questions. What can the witness see on the basis of this document. That's what he should be asked. He shouldn't be led. That's the purpose of my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I haven't ruled on Mr. Krgovic's -- formally ruled on Mr. Krgovic's initial objection which he has refined, because the -- one of the difficulties that I'm still thinking my way through, Ms. Korner, and Mr. Krgovic, is that the question, on the face of it, seems permissible notwithstanding that the Prosecution is asking of its own witness a conclusion drawn from the document. But I -- but -- whereas technically, I suppose, it is leading, the -- it is necessary, in my view, to elicit from the witness the -- his impression, for want of a better word, of the accuracy of the normal inference that could be drawn from the presence of the -- these names on the -- on -- on the payroll sheet at the relevant moment. So I'll permit Ms. Korner to go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I am asking you, on the face of these documents does it appear to you as an experienced police officer that, notwithstanding this complaint, this gentleman remained in the special police until it was wound up in August?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, let's look at another one, shall we, as an example.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look, please, at -- yes. It's paragraph 16 of this long report in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And these are the people who actually appeared on the separate information sheets that we saw. Let's take -- can I say that it is our contention that Mr. Cvetko Makivic stayed through but perhaps it's not -- he was driving maybe in a stolen vehicle and behaved impudently. But let's have a look at Mr. Gojko Racic. On the 20th of June, and, again, this was a subject of a separate report, he threatened an armed attack on the centre. I think you may remember this. He went in and waved his pistol. So if we look now, please, at the payroll again. Oh, it's the first page of the other document, number 10 -- sorry, number 14. There he is. Unless it's -- accepting entirely that there are two people, same name, in the special police, signing for his pay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if you go then on in the long alphabetical list to 197, although -- I'm sorry, I've got the wrong one. That's Radic -- sorry. It's -- I'm not quite sure about that one. Because I think the names -- unless I can't read the ... I cannot read the -- obviously the Cyrillic so ... oh, yes, 190. Sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: He apparently got wounded at some stage.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written here that he was wounded and became disabled.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, would you expect it that the man who came in to the Centar police station, under your command, would be allowed to remain in the special police, if nothing else?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this document is correct, and if these reports are correct, and if he, indeed, behaved in this way, then he -- there should have been no place for him in the organs of internal affairs. But that's a matter for the disciplinary court and the prosecutor. Reports should have been investigated and then he should have been prosecuted, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You see, again, you don't refer to any number of any criminal report you put in, under this paragraph. So did you put in a -- or did your chief of crime police put in a crime report against this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. I think this is the product of some Official Note or maybe a report by the operative duty officer. I -- I see from this that he also behaved himself inappropriately in the centre. What I mean is I don't know what the outcome was. Did we file it to the CSB, and how that was processed, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Can we very quickly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, can I ask you a question in this respect. If a member of your special police force had been involved in some serious criminal activity, such as the example we have seen here with Mr. Racic, and if that would imply that he would be released from duty, at what moment would he then be released? Would that be by the time a criminal report was filed to the prosecutor, or would it be immediately after the incident, or would it not be until the moment when he had finally been convicted, if, let's assume, that he was convicted. So at which time would you dismiss your police officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, we would have to know if Gojko Racic was a member of the reserve force of the special detachment of the CSB Banja Luka or an active duty officer employed full time. If he was in the reserve, then the procedure would be short. He could be taken off the schedule and placed at the disposal of the VRS. However, if he was full-time employee --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Right away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, if he was a reserve member, he could taken off the roster immediately. He would be stripped of his weapons and placed at the disposal of the army. However, if he was an employee, then disciplinary proceedings would have to be taken, and then the prosecutor would have to decide in an initiative that -- with the chief of the centre. This proposal by the prosecutor would go before the disciplinary court which would decide on the measures to be taken. That procedure is not so short. He could also be temporarily suspended pending the completion of disciplinary proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And if you'd had a police officer in your command who had gone into one of your stations and waved a gun, would you have suspended him, pending the proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would do precisely as I explained to the Judge. If he was a reserve member, I would take him -- I would remove him immediately. If he was an employee, I would initiate proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. And the question I asked was: If he was an employee, and you initiated proceedings, would you suspend him, pending the outcome of those proceedings?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in our proposal to initiate disciplinary proceedings to the chief of the centre we would include a proposal for temporary suspension. If everything was confirmed, we would also ask for a temporary sanction.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we very quickly -- and then I'll do one more after this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mrs. Korner, one more question. Mr. Tutus, if a full-time employee was temporarily suspended pending procedures, would he still be paid?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I remember our regulations well he would be receiving 50 per cent of the pay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we look at, please, the next paragraph, 18, Mr. Marinko Marincic, who was -- again, we saw the report. He is stealing petrol.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Again, it doesn't refer to any criminal report being filed. If we look on this occasion, it does not appear in the payroll for August. But if we go to the list, the alphabetical list, and we go to 135, he is the only one of the ones that we're going to go through who was actually relieved of duty in June, for stealing petrol. Well, we don't know why he was -- but the only allegation that we see made against him is that this was stealing petrol. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't yet identified which number it is in this report.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Number -- paragraph --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did you say 11?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: paragraph 18 of your 1993 report.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you repeat the question now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Mr. Marinko Marincic, who we saw the full information report before, he and some other people were caught decanting fuel. And if you look at him, he does not appear in the August payroll. Yes, I made a mistake. And, indeed, it shows that he was relieved of duty. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right, as far as this report is concerned. But whether he was relieved of duty and why, I don't know. This report also says he fled the scene and prevented us from collecting and seizing evidence. And we probably filed this in a report to the CSB, because, according to preliminary information, these persons were members of the special detachment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Now, finally, those four people who were taken out of the prison in July. The whole incident is referred to in your report, I think ... yes. If we look at paragraph 22, the -- the long list of crimes as set out there. And these are -- do you agree, we looked at all the documents around this. These are the people who you wouldn't release but were then taken out of Tunjice prison effectively by force?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: If we look, please, at the payroll for August, number 54, is Mr. Dragojevic. Number 45 is Mr. Jokic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. All right. And very quickly then, and that's the last matter I'm going ask you, if you look at the list of payroll, the -- the special police detachment list, number 40, Mr. Dragojevic who went off to -- I'm not sure what this means, Simic, VP Simic, Captain Luka; and number 77, Mr. Jokic, goes off to the same unit. And it's right, isn't it, if you look at the last page of the payroll for August, the two signatures that appear there are Mr. Samardzija and Stojan Zupljanin. Page 7 of 20. That's it -- no, the payroll for August. That's the ... yeah.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my version, it's page 6. And that's correct. Those are the signatures.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Finally, and this is the last question, did Mr. Zupljanin ever attempt to replace you, Mr. Tutus?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard that from him. Not from him personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Who did you hear it from?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it on one occasion in 1994. Minister Stanisic was answering a question by President Radic in Bijeljina when he said something like that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's all I ask.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Korner. Mr. Zecevic, it's eight minutes before the break, would you wish to begin now or would you prefer to proceed uninterrupted?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm so sorry. Whatever please the Court --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, if you could make use of the eight minutes, I prefer to keep the regular patterns.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, okay. Definitely, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Tutus. Mr. Tutus, you have been a member of the MUP since 1973; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understood your CV, you spent your entire career in the police. You joined the police force immediately after school.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, after primary school, as a cadet, in Vrace, I completed high school and later I joined the -- I joined the force. But that's not my entire life. I still have some life ahead of me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, that's not how I meant it to sound. I'm talking about until 1992, because that's the relevant time for the indictment.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, you became chief of the public security station in Banja Luka by decision of Minister Delimustafic in 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember your interview correctly, and the whole situation, to the best of our understanding, there was a so-called inter-party agreement among the national parties. And according to that agreement, one of the points was that the parties divided among them the senior positions within the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your appointment, or, rather, nomination as chief of the public security station Banja Luka followed after the proposal of the Serbian Democratic Party, although you had not been and did not become later a member of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your appointment, if I may conclude, followed from the fact that you were a professional policeman, and you were deserving of the position.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think those who appointed me are better placed to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. From 1991, when you became chief of the public security station, and I believe even before, I drew the impression from your interview that you were rather disenchanted with the situation within the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was rather dissatisfied.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just before your appointment, you went with other nominees to a meeting with Mr. Avdo Hebib who was then charting the personnel policy of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina in Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were several nominees.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You were invited to that meeting. However, nobody received you. You spent the entire day waiting at the Ministry of the Interior in Sarajevo and nobody eventually received you.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were sitting on the premises of the duty service for around two or three hours. Then they handed us our IDs back. They told us we are free to go back to Banja Luka. There was no one to receive us. I took a break in Sarajevo. Then I returned, and with my official ID, I entered the MUP again and went to see the Assistant Minister Momcilo Mandic and told him the story.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when you complained to Mr. Momcilo Mandic, whom you had known from high school; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you explained to him, he eventually took you to see Mr. Hebib, who was in charge of personnel policy at the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you ended up talking to him.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Momo was obviously unhappy with how things were going and he accompanied me to the office of Mr. Avdo Hebib, who did conduct that interview with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said in your interview that either on that occasion or at -- on some later occasion when you were again in Sarajevo, Mr. Mandic told you that the problem of personnel policy at the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina was extremely serious and that Muslim staff is being hired outside of the staffing specification?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Momcilo said something to that effect, but I can't remember if it was on that day or sometime later.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember if he mentioned perhaps that in one day, 300 letters of appointments were handed to Muslim staff, new Muslim staff?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember he said, Vlado, very weird things are going on here. In the course of the night, after business hours, as many as 200 or 300 employees, Green Berets, stay on who were being hired into the MUP. He mentioned the Green Berets and the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I see the time, Your Honours, and I think this is appropriate time to break. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So we resume in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, if I have understood your testimony correctly and the interview that you gave to the Prosecution, at the time the SJB in Banja Luka, not only that SJB, didn't receive sufficient equipment, uniforms, pistols from the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you also emphasised the fact that you didn't have a sufficient amount of vehicles. You didn't even have a single four-wheel drive; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the same period of time, your subordinate chiefs of police stations in Mejdan and Budzak, if I remember your interview correctly, at one point in time, in 1991, they went to Sarajevo on their own initiative without even informing you of the fact; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And upon returning from Sarajevo, they both brought a new car with them, one new car each, some equipment. They started doing work on reconstructing the police station, Mejdan and Budzak. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mejdan and Budzak, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood you correctly, you asked them to come and speak to you. Could you briefly tell us what you discussed, when they returned from Sarajevo and when you found out that they had been to Sarajevo without having informed you of the fact. Could you briefly tell us what the discussion was about.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at the beginning of 1992. On Friday, they took the train to Sarajevo, and on Saturday and Sunday, they received a Volkswagen Golf each from the Ministry of the Interior. I found out about this on Monday. When other senior officers informed me of what had happened, I called them into my office and asked them whether this was correct. They showed me the documents for the goods. They showed me that they had brought a Volkswagen Golf in each and they had also received some equipment, shoes, shirts, uniforms, I'm not sure whether there were any weapons. I asked them why they had done this without informing me. I said that was an inappropriate way of proceeding in the MUP. They told me they had gone to Sarajevo upon the authorisation of Chief Zupljanin. I contacted Chief Zupljanin and he told me that it was correct, that he had agreed to this. He had spoken to the minister about the matter. I think that's what was said. I then told him this was not right. How could they receive such equipment? They said they went to see their own men. I said, What do you mean? Which man, who? And then the commander of the Mejdan police station said that he went to see Avdo Hebib on a party basis, and the other person said that he went to see Kvesic, if I remember this correctly. Then I ordered them to hand in the vehicles to the traffic police centre because they needed it more than these two individuals, and that's what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just clarify something. The chief of the police station in Mejdan was a Muslim and a SDA party member, is that correct, that's why he went to see Avdo Hebib?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say "chief." We're talking about the commanders of these police stations. But, yes, what you have said is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the Budzak police station was a Croat, and he went to see Branko Kvesic, who was one of the leaders of the MUP in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. He was appointed by the HDZ. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if it's not a problem to add this, when I found out about all of this, I sent him a letter and I informed the minister of the interior of the matter, the deputy minister of the interior, the assistant of the minister for crime, and the chief of the CSB. In that letter, I expressed my dissatisfaction with the procedure and I said that the Banja Luka SJB had a lot of problems with materiel and equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The dispatch, the letter you sent to the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, in which you complained about such appropriation for personal needs, such appropriation of equipment, such a way of providing police stations with equipment, well, did you ever receive an explanation or an answer to that dispatch that you sent?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Wouldn't it be true to say that -- well, the commanders of the Mejdan and Budzak police stations were Muslims and Croats, but the commander of the Centar police station was a Serb. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in your interview I think you said you asked these two men, when you asked them to come and speak to you, on Monday, when you found out that they had been in Sarajevo, you asked them why they hadn't taken the commander of the Centar police station with them. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What did they answer?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they both said that they went to see their men in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me if I have understood the matter correctly, these police stations or, rather, the commanders of the police stations in Mejdan and Budzak also started renovating those police stations. They started painting them and so on.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They obtained certain equipment, some paint that had been brought into the police station. I was then informed of the fact and then I phoned them and prohibited that they started receiving this from certain donors. That was not appropriate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the time did you have the impression that there was discrimination, a certain amount of discrimination against Serbian staff in the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina and in SJBs or, rather, in police stations headed by Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say it was a difficult situation in the -- within the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you would agree with me that there were certain differences when it came to treating Serb staff in police stations, police stations and SJBs headed by Serbs. They weren't treated in the same way as staff who were of Muslim or Croat nationality?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously there was a party influence within the Ministry of the Interior. That was quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Isn't it true that towards the end of 1991, or, rather, in 1992, a decision was taken on separating the municipalities of Stari Grad and Ivanjska in the territory of the town of Banja Luka. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I have understood you, a decision was taken. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Before the war broke out there was an initiative in Banja Luka according to which the municipality of Banja Luka should be broken down in an administrative sense and divided into a number of municipalities. And that was still current four or five years ago. Then after the multi-party elections, individual political parties wanted to again divide Banja Luka into a number of municipalities, and the town assembly was against this idea and they did not permit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is it true that this was a joint initiative of the SDA and HDZ parties, a joint initiative to form the municipalities of Stari Grad, Bronzan and Mejdan, Krupa, Vrbas, Stricici, and Ivanjska in the territory of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, more or less. Instead of Stari Grad, I think they mentioned Mejdan as one of the possible municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that if the municipalities were reorganised in that way, some of the newly formed municipalities would then have one of the peoples in the majority. The Muslim people or the Croat people would be in the majority in that case. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At the time, the situation in Krajina, in terms of security, was very difficult; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I have understood your comments in your interview correctly, there was a certain amount of psychoses that was the result of the shelling of certain towns. Gradiska, for example, and Brod from the territory of Croatia. And many Serbian refugees had arrived from the territory of Croatia and this caused a certain amount of tension, certain difficulties. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At the time you know that the SDA party sent candidates that it selected, Muslim candidates, of course, to be trained in the MUP of the Republic of Croatia. Are you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about this, but I have no direct information about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember that in a decision, or, rather, an order from Minister Delimustafic the reserve of police force was mobilised in September 1991?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it true that you arrived at the conclusion that the SDA, or, rather, the Ministry of the Interior, was trying to form an army from the police in that manner; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was quite obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please provide us with a detailed explanation - I think this will also assist the Chamber and everyone else in the courtroom - how is the reserve police force mobilised? Could you briefly explain this for us.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reserve police force is mobilised in extraordinary circumstances, when there is an imminent threat of war and in the course of war. The minister of the interior has to issue an order for their mobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For someone to become a member of the reserve police force in the former Yugoslavia, in the SFRY, it was obligatory to perform one's military service; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The Secretariat of -- municipal secretariats for municipal defence, for All People's Defence had to send young men of 18 and over to do their military service. It was their responsibility. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After they had completed their military service, the person who had completed his military service would then bring in his case file from the unit that he was a member of and there was evidence of the fact that the person had certain training, specialist knowledge, obtained in the course of his military training. This was called VES.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it was called. But what you call the case file, I think they were called unit files and they were sent from military units to the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So someone who completed his military service would then return to his place of domicile and would have to report to the municipal organ, the municipal military organ of national defence that had sent that person to serve in the army and the person would have to inform that body that his military training had been completed. Documents would be produced to that effect, and at that point in time, that Secretariat for National Defence would categorise that person as a member of the military reserve force. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He would be inscribed as a conscript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When the police need certain reserve policemen, with certain specialities, then the SJB or the CSB would contact the municipal organ for national defence with a request to, for example, provide the personnel files for certain individuals you needed and to have them transferred to the police reserve force from the military reserve force. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. May I add an explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please let us observe pauses between questions and answers to avoid problems with the record.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as transfers are concerned from military departments to the police, certain vetting is -- is needed. If we needed 20 men, we would ask for 30 and then we would choose those who have no criminal records and who pass our field screening, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You anticipated another question I wanted to ask. So you would ask for a larger number than you actually needed. The Secretariat for National Defence would provide you with a certain number of candidates according to the specialities you required, and then you would conduct screening, and only those who meet the requirements to become members of the reserve police would be chosen. And then you would inform the military department and the Secretariat for National Defence that you would transfer that particular number of men who satisfy all the criteria to the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then these men continued to be on file as reserve policemen attached to a public security station on a particular list; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. With a proviso that these men would undergo certain training, according to the plan adopted by the Ministry of the Interior. The training plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this professional training is refreshed at certain intervals?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A programme would be reviewed and adopted every year, and it would be implemented every year.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In situations like the one you were facing, with the immediate threat of war and high security risks, you, in the police, regardless of the already-existing reserve police force, if you needed an additional number of reserve policemen, you would again, as we described, approach the municipal Secretariat for National Defence and would again ask for a new list of candidates; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When these men become reserve policemen, when they are transferred to the reserve police force, their individual personnel files would be transferred to the archive of the MUP; that is, of the particular public security station.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We will now move to a different subject.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't know if any outstanding questions remain regarding the reserve and the transfer of reserve soldiers to the reserve police force. Is there anything further I need to clarify for the Chamber?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Not -- thank you, Mr. Zecevic. We're satisfied. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My colleague reminds me about one fact that is still important to clarify. At the moment when, for whatever reason, you take off a certain individual from the list of your reserve police, you return his personal file to the municipal Secretariat for National Defence and you inform them that he had been taken off the roster of the reserve police and that he is back at their disposal.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. We would inform them there is no further need for that person's engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the first day of your examination-in-chief, my learned friend asked you about the meeting in Banja Luka of 11 February 1992. It's 1D135. And the tab number, according to the list we provided, is 126.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we have prepared two binders of hard-copy documents for the witness, and since the witness does not have good eye-sight, it is up to him to choose whether he would be viewing documents in hard copy or on the monitor. I thought would be fair to give him the paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Of course, Mr. Zecevic. Thank you. Thank you for your assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, now have you copies of all of the documents before you. This is one number 126. I believe it's in binder number 2. Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I understood your evidence correctly, you had never seen this record of the meeting before.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw it when it was shown to me by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You couldn't even remember that meeting specifically, so we won't go through it. However, on page 4 of that document, there is a record of your contribution to the discussion. And I believe when the Prosecution showed that you document, you said you could not remember everything accurately but as far as the facts you presented, such as that you were lacking an all-terrain vehicle, et cetera, you confirmed that that was, indeed, the situation.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, do you remember, on page 2, the contribution of Mr. Stanisic is summarised, and in the second paragraph on that page, page 2, it says: "From this meeting, it is needed to collect a minimum of outstanding requests to be sent to Minister Delimustafic with a reasonable deadline to deal with them." Do you remember that there was, indeed, a suggestion that the demands made at the meeting should be submitted to the minister so that the outstanding issues be resolved within a reasonable time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right now I can't remember, but I don't see any reason why that shouldn't be right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me, won't you, that this document demonstrates the seriousness and the complexity of security problems that existed at the time in the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Especially within the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, bearing in mind what we discussed at the very beginning, the situations that you witnessed personally, those trips to Sarajevo, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document is tab 1, P527, also shown to you by my learned friend. Tab 1 in the first binder.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: One. It's a letter dated 13 February 1992. On the right-hand side, you see the number of the document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, when you commented this document in response to Ms. Korner's question, you said it also reflects the complexity of the problems that existed at the time at the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Do you remember that comment?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What I want to know, Mr. Tutus, although you were not a recipient of this document, judging by its format, it looks like an official dispatch sent by the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It looks official.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Each and every official dispatch of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is copied to the archives of the same MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That is governed by the rules of the service.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If there is an official dispatch sent by the regular channels of communication, by teletype, then it's certainly not a secret dispatch, is it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I now ask for P323, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a dispatch dated 31st March 1992, signed by Assistant Minister of the Interior, Momcilo Mandic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P353, I'm sorry. Binder 1, tab 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Tutus, I did not want to confuse you; I wanted to help you. But if you find it easier, look at the monitor.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This document was shown to you earlier by Ms. Korner, and you confirmed that you had received this document.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember exactly, but if I confirmed, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you're certainly familiar with the substance.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After that, my learned friend Ms. Korner showed you another document, a dispatch from the minister, Alija Delimustafic, 1D136, tab 4. That's the next document for you. 1D136 of the same date.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember giving comments on this document to Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Ms. Korner asked you if you had done anything about this document from Alija Delimustafic; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you answered that you had not done anything particular about that document. However, on page 72 of your interview, and earlier in your evidence here, you did hold meetings about these documents we looked at, dated 31st March 1992. You did go with one of your assistants to special meetings, to the police station Mejdan and the Budzak police station, both.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that it was your evidence here, too, that at the meeting, first in Budzak where the commander of the police station was a Croat, once you've explained to them the situation that had arisen, as a result of the decision to divide the MUP, some of the policemen of Croat ethnicity asked you if that meant that they were supposed to work with criminals, and your response was that this was not going to happen while you were there. You had invited them to stay in their jobs and join the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A handful of them refused to sign the solemn declaration and left the premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At page 72 of your interview, and I only wish you to confirm that this is, indeed, what -- the way I'm going paraphrase it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I just want to know where the word "a handful" only refused appear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner it's the answer of the -- of the witness. It wasn't -- it wasn't suggested by me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I thought you were quoting the -- the answer in the interview that the witness gave. And I can't see the words "a handful" anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, the -- no, it is 45, 22, the witness answer was: "Yes, a handful of them refused to sign the solemn declaration and left the premises."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I see. So you weren't saying that's what he said in interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No. That is the answer of the witness.
