utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, no, I just wanted to know whether you were putting that from the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In your interview, you said: "I was asked by one of the policemen in Budzak, Chief, are you going to guarantee that criminals would not be working with us?" And you said: "Yes, I can give you that guarantee for as long as I am the chief." "And the Croat, who I believe was from Ivanjska, said, If you give us that guarantee, then we will trust you and stay with you." And that's what you've just confirmed a moment ago. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The interview goes on to say: "The commander of the police station stood up and said, and I will paraphrase to the best of my recollection: I will not have the three-colour insignia on my cap. How am I going to go to the villages inhabited with Croats with such a uniform? What would they tell me? And I am calling upon all of those who share my view to leave the meeting. A couple of them stood up and left with him. All the rest stayed at the meeting, and I closed it. There were no problems. The soldiers -- those who had weapons returned them and that's how it was."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter notes that the three-colour insignia was the Serbian three-colour insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't see that the witness answer was recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Will you please repeat your answer. It is not reflected in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 68 of your interview, in answer to a question put by the OTP, you presented certain percentages as to how many of all the members of the public security station Banja Luka of Muslim and Croat ethnicities, and we're including the Centar, Mejdan and Budzak police stations into that station, had remained in the area. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your answer at the time was that of all the Croat members of the public security station Banja Luka who, on the 31st of March, when the MUP was divided, were working for the MUP, 73 per cent agreed to stay with the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. Of all the Croats -- I don't need to go on explaining if the matter is clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But you may clarify, just in case. In other words, if there were 100 of them, let's say, 73 stayed in their job.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And 27 left MUP or, rather, refused to work for the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Compared to the number of Muslims, the percentage was 61; is that right? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is that piece of information correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us clarify this fully. Of 100 Muslims who worked there, 61 agreed to go on working for the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, by way of an example.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, just an example.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I think we should make it clear, though, that this comes from an article in "Glas" where he is quoted, and we should have the date as well, and I think the document should go in. It's an article from "Glas" dated the 24th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner, I don't intend to use the newspaper articles because you know my --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then you can't use -- you can't have it both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, no, but I have -- I have asked the witness and he confirmed these -- these numbers. I don't see why would I additionally need to put an article on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Because it is not clear from the question and answer that these are answers that he gave to a reporter as quoted by a reporter. I don't believe he has any other document to support this assertion.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is not based on a document. This is based on his knowledge and he -- in his interview on page 68, he -- I will read the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, could you read the question at line 3 on page 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, and he said this is true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The question was -- for the illustration 73 per cent of the Croat and 65 Muslim -- 65 -- 61 per cent of the Muslim of -- of the existing number of employees have agreed to -- to -- to -- to stay. And he says that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what is actually put to him is -- by the investigator, Let me show you a -- well, it's a "Glas" article dated the 24th of April, 1992, written by Mr. Kopanja, entitled: "Lies for War Psychoses." And then it's put to him that: "You apparently declare to the journalist" and then the figures are put, and he agrees with that. That's what he said to the journalist. So it is not quite the same thing. Can I -- that's the difference I'm trying to draw.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me rephrase my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, do you recall as the truth that 73 per cent of Croats, members of the MUP of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, after the 1st of April, agreed to stay on in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Yes or no, to the best of your recollection.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd very much like to see an article or anything else that might substantiate it, but I have no reason to doubt the information if it was published, as it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I don't have the reference. I don't have a problem if -- that we show the document to the witness. If -- if Ms. Korner can help with me with that, I would appreciate. Or over the break I can provide this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... I mean, that it is not that he was quoting statistics. It's -- this is the -- the journalist says, "This is what you said," and he says, "I agree." So that's the only small point I'm trying to make.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I have had the impression until the witness's last answer that, notwithstanding that the source of this was this article in "Glas," that he -- effectively adopted it, the figures, and made them his own. But now I'm not sure as to ... It probably may be necessary, if -- if this is an important point to go back to the source material.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I will prepare the document after the break, and then I will revisit the issue with the witness. If that pleases the Court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now that the issue of newspaper articles has been raised, two days ago, my learned friend showed you the 4th of April, 1992, "Glas" article, which is P536. You don't have it in the binder there, but you will see it on the monitor.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This it P536.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You commented on the article, which was published about the SOS action in Banja Luka. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As I was preparing my questions for you, I noticed that, on page 1 of the document, at the very bottom, it is stated that all the members of the Islamic faith were to receive greetings on the occasion of the Bajram festivities, and this has not been translated into English. Do you see this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To all the members of Islamic faith and what follows is a "Mubarek Bajram, Mubarek Olsun," which is probably the expression used on the occasion of the Bajram feast. Is that right.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There were several questions put in relation to the reasons behind or the motivations behind this event between the 4th and the 5th of April, 1992, in Banja Luka. I would like to take you back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And I would like the top part to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Where the very article describes the reasons prompting the event.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please turn to the left. Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As can you see, it states here the motivation for the action is Jerko Doko's address, a minister in the government of the Bosnia-Herzegovina, and his statement that the reservists were waging a private war and placing themselves outside the law. In other words, the SOS members thus presented the reasons for their actions. Do you recall the statement by Jerko Doko made in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, Jerko Doko was the minister of defence in the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina. During this period of time a dispatch was sent to the heads of public security stations, where we were asked to take out unit dossiers from the various offices for national defence in order to prevent the JNA from mobilising people. We felt that this did not fall within our competence, to engage in such activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I'm well informed, Mr. Jerko Doko was a Croat and a member of the HDZ, was he not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was member of the HDZ or not, but I do believe that he was a Croat and the minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness be shown page 2 of the article. Could we zoom in on the top part of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here, again, in this box, it is stated that the blockade of the Banja Luka area carried out by the "Serbian Defence Forces," in inverted commas, is the result of the address by Jerko Doko, minister of defence of Bosnia-Herzegovina, to the National Assembly of Banja Luka, who had accused of -- who had accused the reservists of waging a private war. Is this what you've been referring to a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At one point the Prosecutor asked you if you had participated in the negotiations with the Serb Defence Forces, et cetera, and you -- your answer was negative. At the very bottom it is stated that after several hours of negotiations where members of the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka and members of the Banija Luka Corps, the JNA, and of -- and the AR Krajina took part -- 8

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you please not move the article because we were focussing on the middle of the page in order for the witness to follow. Right. Thank you. I will have to read it anew. Can the page -- can we turn to the left of the page a bit so that we can see the start of the column. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is stated: "After several hours of negotiations between representatives of the Crisis Staff of Banja Luka, Territorial Defence, the JNA's Banija Luka Corps, and institutions of lawful authorities in Banja Luka, the demands put forth," et cetera. Not even the newspaper article seems to mention that MUP representatives, representatives of the CSB, participated in this in any way.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my statement that I did not take part in this at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now be shown a video that has already been seen. It's the parade dated the 13th of May. P1080 is the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But before we show the video, could you please comment on something? The 13th of May, in the former Yugoslavia, was the date of the so-called Security Day. Members of the security services celebrated this day. Members of the MUP and members of military security celebrated this day. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. With your permission, festivities were large-scale festivities. There were large-scale gatherings that were held in various towns, in different towns every year, and I'm proud to be able to say that I participated in most of those gatherings, most of those celebrations, well, for at least ten or 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And these assemblies, so to speak, were held both at the federal level and at the level of all the republics and regions in the former Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the level of municipalities right up to the federal level.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it was customary for the Republican Secretariat for the interior -- the republican secretary for the interior, that would now correspond to the role of minister, it was customary for that person to inspect the members of the security services. An appropriate speech would be given. Then there were versus cultural and artistic programmes, sports events and so on and so forth. That was the nature of the celebrations. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please show the video. P1080. I apologise, I didn't think that it was for us to show the video. I haven't prepared that, so I will do so during the break. I do apologise. Mr. Smith says that he will be kind enough to show it for our benefit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: My question concerns the end. You can continue showing it. In the course of your testimony, you confirmed that this equipment -- this military equipment, they are military vehicles we can see here. That was in response to a question from Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Towards the end --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could Mr. Smith show the part where the helicopters appear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I also had this question for the witness about these APCs that are driving down on the street, and I wonder if it is possible to -- to go back and try and enlarge the white script that is on one of the blue APCs, I think, the second or the third. I'm not sure if it says "policija," but it looks to me as if it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Even better. Then can we see it, if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Can I return back, because this is a perfect spot for what I want to show to the witness on this and then I will return. If it pleases the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the helicopters were a subject of discussion and you confirmed that the Banja Luka CSB, before 1992, had one helicopter which -- well, you said there was a heli-port and you said that the helicopter was used for the needs of the MUP or, rather, the CSB. Isn't that what you said?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. That helicopter was obtained for the needs of the municipal secretariat for internal affairs, which later back the SJB. And later, this all became part of the CSB. It was all integrated at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But it is true to say that that helicopter isn't one of these helicopters because the helicopter that the Banja Luka CSB had before 1992 was taken to Sarajevo. Isn't that correct? That's what you said?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know how this was done. I don't know whether it was handed over or sold. I don't know how this was done, but I know that we lost the helicopter.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at the photograph on the screen now, please. Isn't it true that when you have a look at the tail-end of the helicopter, you can see a red star, a five-pointed star, and that's the symbol of the JNA, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If we can further play the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Stop here. Sorry. If can you just return here. Yeah, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see it now?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that very clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Isn't it correct to say that that is the symbol used by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the five-pointed star.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Smith, I appreciate your help very much but can we go back now for -- for the -- to this -- to the very beginning for the purposes of the question for -- Judge Harhoff posed. Yeah. Can you stop here? Would it be -- well, maybe -- maybe a further on a bit. Yeah, here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can you see that it says "milicija" here in the Cyrillic script?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, would you want me to -- I have another question on this matter and maybe later if you would like me to pursue the matter any further.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: I won't. Please move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, isn't it true to say that these -- as you say, military vehicles, and I agree with that description, these military vehicles were quite recently painted blue. You can see that.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Even the wheels were painted blue?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, or you would agree with me, would you not, that these vehicles and this entire parade was in fact held for propaganda purposes. The vehicles were used for propaganda purposes and the parade was held for propaganda purposes?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say so. I think the purpose was to demonstrate force and to demonstrate, for the benefit of the citizens, that the situation was secure, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's what I meant by propaganda purposes as well. Thank you. I said that that's what I meant when I said propaganda purposes as well. Let's go back to 1D150 now. 1D151. These are documents that you will find in the second binder. 130 and 131 are the numbers in your binder. This is document 1D150, signed by the minister for internal affairs, Alija Delimustafic. It was forwarded to all CSBs, to public security stations, and it has to do with an order issued by the commander of the Territorial Defence Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, dated the 29th of April, 1992. It's an order on implementing a Presidency decision, in fact. Do you remember this document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Amongst other things, under item 1 the document states the following: "All roads in the territory of the [Realtime transcript read in error "Republic of Serbia"] Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina being used by units of the former JNA for pulling out materiel and equipment are to be completely blocked in direct coordination with the Ministry of the Interior." Item 2: "Larger areas with military installations, et cetera." Item 3: "Unannounced convoys of former JNA units and convoys without MUP escorts shall not be allowed to leave the barracks, et cetera." Item 4 says: "Urgently plan and launch combat activities throughout the territory of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and these activities are to be coordinated with the Territorial Defence staffs of the region, districts and the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina ..." Do you remember this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You would agree with me that this document is, in fact, an order on starting a war.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's not what I would say. My opinion is that this order was supposed to cause a conflict between the JNA on the one side and the police and the Territorial Defence on the other. And that's what I said with regard to that transcript. I said there were ugly dispatches from the MUP. This is one of the ugliest ones that I received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As an objection to the transcript, page 58, line 14, it says the Republic of Serbia, but the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is concerned. That's what it says in the document itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, if you are about to move on to something else, it's 12.05.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: 20 minutes [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, let us conclude our discussion on this document concerning Alija Delimustafic and the 29th of April. You said that, in your view, the document, had paved the way to a conflict between the JNA, TO, and the police. And the truth of the matter is that the conflict did take place, did it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have to go back to the issue we discussed at the start of my examination concerning the percentages of Muslims and Croats who remained with the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina after the MUP had separated on the 31st of March. We prepared the article from "Glas."

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If the Usher would be so kind to -- to give the copy of the document to the witness. Your Honours, may I just inform the Court that it has been uploaded in the e-court. It is 1D03-2165.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Thank you [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As can you see, sir, this is an article from "Glas"; page 2 of the 24th of April, 1992. In the box, the text refers to strong reactions to some statements by Muharem Krzic, president of the Party of Democratic Action for Banja Luka. The last four paragraphs relate your statement. I quote: "Krzic's statements have provoked strong reactions in the Banja Luka public station -- security station as well?" And then let's skip a bit. And here, apparently your words are related: "Mr. Muharem Krzic has for a while now systematically been attacking the CSB and the SJB of Banja Luka. In my view, these are thought-out fabrications in order to create an atmosphere of war in these -- in this area." And then you go on to say that Mr. Krzic does not hesitate to use any sort of means to demean the SJB. So, he stated that out of the 105 policemen, only 7 Muslims and 6 Croats were employed. Although the public at large knows that such statements are pure fabrications and lies. "'For illustration's sake,'" you go on to say, "'the loyalty oath,'" and when you say the "loyalty oath," I suppose you're referring to the solemn declaration, "'to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina had so far been signed by 73 per cent of Croats and 61 per cent of Muslims of the overall number of members of our SJB,' Vladimir Tutus stated, the chief of the SJB Banja Luka." Mr. Tutus, do you recall stating this and do you stand by what you said at the time?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What strikes me is that Mr. Muharem Krzic, the president of the SDA Banja Luka, as early as the 18th of March, stated that only seven Muslims and six Croats were employed for the Banja Luka SJB. And this is something that was referred to here. The 18th of March precedes the date of the separation of the MUP, does it not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I hope this satisfies the -- the issue of knowledge of this witness concerning the percentages of Muslim and Croat workers in the -- who remained in -- in MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: It certainly does, Mr. Zecevic. Although one little question could be added to the questions that you have put. Namely, how long did the two gentlemen stay in office in the SJBs that we discussed earlier this morning? There was specific reference made to two named chiefs of SDBs -- SJBs, one was a Croat and the other was a Muslim, who stayed in office, who stayed and continued to serve as chief of the SJB, even after they had not signed the -- the declaration and even after the MUP was split. So my question was -- that's very good, that proves your point, but how long did they continue to stay in office? Right through the end of the conflict?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if I may remind you. First of all, it refers to commanders of the police stations, Mejdan and Budzak, and I believe the witness has said that on this meeting, when he went over there, both of them resigned on that particular meeting and they didn't stay. Both of them. Both commanders of Mejdan and Budzak have resigned and they didn't stay on the force after the 31st of March, but can I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- ask the witness to confirm that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: You are right. I was wrong. My recollection simply fooled me here. So you don't need to pursue. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would suggest that this now needs to be an exhibit, the whole article, because the context is important.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, you know the position of the Stanisic Defence concerning newspaper articles. I don't think that -- that the document needs to be exhibited and neither will we offer it for exhibit, because I believe the witness sufficiently stated that it his recollection and that he stays by this.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, no. I mean, with respect, that can't be right. The context of all of this is important. That's why I raised the question of the fact that it came from a newspaper article. The Defence are using newspaper articles when it suits them and other newspaper articles are admitted into evidence as exhibits, and indeed the witness said that's what he said and he stands by it. So it is an accurate quote.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the article is derivative and the evidence, as Mr. Zecevic has said, is what the witness has testified to here so what's the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, no, Your Honour, that's not right, and with respect. What he says is this accurately quotes what he says. In -- in the submission of the Prosecution, the context of this whole quote is important and the context is given by the article. And articles are admissible in -- in evidence and have been so admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, of course, that has happened. But are you talking in terms of this specific article, having regard to the testimony that we have heard, I -- I -- I am still at a loss as to why, in the Prosecution's view, it needs be exhibited. On the other hand, I don't see any harm to it being exhibited having regard to the fact that articles have been exhibited. So ...

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I don't mind. If Mr. Zecevic won't ask formally for to it to be exhibited in his case, then I'm going do so in reexamination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I definitely will not offer this document because we take the principled position out of -- as a principle. So -- but I don't object that Ms. Korner uses in the cross-examination [sic] and offers it to -- for -- to evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I continue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, I would now like to discuss the work of the Banja Luka public security station which you were at the head of in 1992, since this is relevant for our case. In the course of your testimony, you said, on several occasions, that communications in the course of 1992 - that's to say, as of the month of April onwards - with the Ministry of the Interior, were quite difficult. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your communication with the SCB [as interpreted] Banja Luka was not difficult since you were housed in the same building. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: However, the communication with the ministry did experience problems, as you said. Is it not the case that even in physical terms, Krajina had been cut off up until the month of July from the rest of Bosnia-Herzegovina? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can I just assist Mr. Zecevic in the transcript for once. The question: "Your communication," it was translated as "SCB" but it's clearly you were saying CSB, "was not difficult, since you were housed in the same building. Is that correct?" Well, no word has come out in the transcript but I'm assuming you said "CSB" in Serbian?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I said, "Your communication with the CSB Banja Luka," yes. Thank you, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, I would like to -- you to look at document 65 ter 227, which is behind tab 37. This is a dispatch of the public security station of Banja Luka, chief of department, Mr. Josic signed it, and the date is the 21st of August, 1992. This is in response to the -- to the CSB Banja Luka dispatch of the 19th of August. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The information has been given, I suppose, in response to a request from the CSB concerning the number of individuals who were placed in detention between the 1st of January, 1992, and the 20th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is stated here that the -- that detention was imposed by the public security station against 172 individuals; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that the individuals who were placed in detention up to -- through -- three days were within the time-limit of 72 hours turned over to the -- to the -- investigating judge having jurisdiction, together with reports and criminal reports. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And according to your section chief, there was not a single complaint filed against the work of the section in placing individuals in detention in the course of the said period. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was that, indeed, the situation in the Banja Luka SJB as reflected here?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This section chief, Zoran Josic, was the chief of the crime police section, was he not, of the CID?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, you are familiar with the information contained in this document and you confirm it, do you not?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this document into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D197, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: -- you have these documents two times in your binder, under tab 37 and tab 108. May I suppose that is a simple mistake?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Definitely, Your Honours. But we have been listing all the documents and we acknowledge that there was some duplicates, and we're not offering them. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, the results of the SJB in 1992, its performance, compared to the performance of the same station in 1991 was, objectively speaking, identical or even improved.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't identical. It was improved.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you clarify, please.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, more than 50 per cent of the criminal cases were resolved, even though the overall number of crimes increased. I think that the station had to deal with over a thousand crimes, which was much more than in the previous period.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understood you correctly. My understanding was that you said that in 1992 there were a thousand crimes that the -- overall number of crimes had been increased by 1.000 compared to 1991.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were more cases in 1992, and the station had to address these cases with the same number of staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To make matters quite clear, you know that we have to have this interpreted and we're having difficulties with the transcript. So if in 1991, as an example, there were 500 crimes, in 1992, there were 1.500 and you had the same staff levels in the public security station Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, we were dealing with thousands of offences.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please turn to tab 67, 1D00-1257. This is an operative work-plan of the Banja Luka CSB. It is classified as an official secret. The date is the 25th of May, 1992. The preamble refers to it being based on the instruction on conducting affairs in crime prevention and detection, which had been applied since 1982 but was still in application in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At page 5 of the operative work-plan, as will you see, it is stated that the plan was drafted by the inspectors of the OZSK section inspectors. I don't know if you recognise the signature in the left-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Whose signature is it under the chief of section?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of the general crime section, Zivko Bojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on the right-hand side, under "Approved"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of centre, Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You are aware of the existence of this document, this operative work-plan. I suppose it involved also your staff at the public security station Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember that we consulted and agreed this activity with the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us go through this document briefly. Again, back to page 1. We read that in the period of less than two months, from 2 or 3 April 1992 until the 25th of May, armed groups and individuals committed 51 robberies. And it lists all the kinds of robberies that were committed. And then it says from mid-August, I suppose it's August 1991, there were 76 incidents involving explosives. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Remember when we talked about robberies? It confirms what you said. By comparison, only nine robberies were committed in 1991, and now just in two months there are 51.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And at the bottom of page 1, it says there indicia that the persons are linked to a number of murders and attempted murders, such as the murder of Mirsad Sabic and the attempted murder of certain Slobodan Tesanjovic. It says also what is needed to be done, to deal with these crimes, to shed light on these cases. 1, to establish a list of criminals who were engaged in SOS units through the mediation of a certain person nicknamed Canak. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And then under (b): "Arrest Mladen Josic." Under (c): Identify a man named Ratko Keser. And then in item 2, disarm and arrest the group led by Brane Palackovic, in brackets, VP military post, where they are posted, et cetera. And then we have several persons enumerated. It also says disarm the group from Starcevica, and so on and so forth. It goes on to item (g), all the various measures envisaged by this operative work-plan. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you agree with me that these measures, under 1, and 2, from (a) to (g), that end on page 3, have for the most part been carried out, to the best of your recollection?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The plan was implemented and I know that there had been arrests and remands in custody.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3, there is another reference to the case of the murder of Sabic, Mirsad. I suppose it's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And towards the bottom of that page, there's a new reference to explosions and the investigation of a series of explosions committed by a group led by Vedran Mandic. You remember that Ms. Korner showed you some documentation concerning this Vedran Mandic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry, to be accurate, I didn't show him documentation. I asked him about the attack on the police station and he mentioned him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Korner. I -- you mentioned Mr. Vedran Mandic. That was the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the last page, page 5 of this document, it says that within the framework of the operative work-plan, in paragraph 2, that investigation is ongoing concerning the explosion at the Arnaudija mosque, and certain operative information is mentioned.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which passage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Paragraph 2. It says work to investigate the explosion around the mosque Arnaudija. It says according to operative information, the explosive was detonated by a certain Milomir Cutkovic, nicknamed Piga, and another person. And it refers also to a note made on the 23rd of March, 1992.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this case about the explosion at the mosque?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph it says: "In view of the fact that these individuals were in a way self-organised in the guise of membership in the SOS, that they are well-armed, and that some of them were mobilised by the JNA, their arrest should be carried out by members of the special police detachment, together with the military police." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in conclusion, it says, I quote: "As long as the military prosecution office and the military court are not finally established, the plan cannot be implemented because most of the offenders are conscripts and members of the former TO, which is why civilian courts and prosecutors refuse to take up these cases." Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember facing this problem at the time because the military prosecutor's office was not operating?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There were such problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And finally, it says the plan would be amended and expanded as needed in the course of each separate operation. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In an attachment to this document, we have a list. In fact, a table with a breakdown of various crimes committed. I believe it's page 6 in e-court, 6 and onwards. It contains the sequential number, the location of the crime, the type of crime, time of perpetration, injured parties, items stolen, and possible perpetrators. And then under number 2 is a certain injured party, Enes Nurkic. Can you see that on page 1? Robberies committed by uniformed persons. The injured party is Enes Nurkic.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which number?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Number 2. I suppose it's a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sulejman Huskic, number 3?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Also Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Number 4, Nermin Osmic also?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean, Nermina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: 6, 7 and 8 are also all Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And number 11, Fikret Velic, also a Muslim citizen?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All these were documented robberies against injured parties of Muslim ethnicities -- ethnicity in the territory of Banja Luka between the 2nd of April and 25 May 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, under numbers 13, 14, 15 -- or, rather, 13 and 14, I believe, are Muslims; 15 is Ivica Paponja [phoen], I suppose a Croat.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The same applies to number 21 and number 22. Croats and Muslims. Do you agree?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page we have, in handwriting, names of injured parties are added. 31, the last name is Sotric.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marzada Sabic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And 32, Denis Hamidovic or Haridovic. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Hamidzic, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Both of them are Muslims.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, numbers 36, 37, and 38, Mahmutovic Spahic, Midhat Obradovac, and number 40, Muslija Dzevad, also Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So if I understand this correctly, the conclusion that simply imposes itself from this operative work-plan is that the CSB Banja Luka and the public security station of Banja Luka were documenting and proceeding on all cases, regardless of the identity and ethnicity of the injured parties.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this is in keeping with your legal obligation under the Law on Internal Affairs of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, if there is no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D198, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, just to show that this operative work-plan was not simply a dead letter on paper, we will show some of the documents that resulted from the implementation of this plan. Open, please, 84. The document is 1D00-1837. It's a letter from the Security Services Centre, signed by chief of sector Djuro Bulic, submitted on 6 July 1992 to the public prosecutor's office in Banja Luka. It reports on proceedings by the CSB.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was not actually signed by Djuro Bulic. It was signed by the chief of the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You recognise Mr. Zupljanin's signature?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the next page, you will see in this document a decision to remind -- to remand in custody - and the date is 3rd July 1992 - to remand in custody Dragan Javorac, Mladen Josic and some other persons?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you remember the previous document we were looking at, in the item 2, (a), it says disarm and arrest the group led by a certain Brano Jackovac [as interpreted], including Dragan Javorac, one Milasinovic and some other persons on this same list. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on page 2 of this decision to remand in custody, signed by Mr. Zupljanin, on page 2 in the reasoning it says: "There are grounds for suspicion that the detained persons, in a group and individually, committed 37 crimes of robbery, murder, extortion, causing public danger, and others ..."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't think it is in dispute that all these persons remanded in custody herewith are of Serb ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, I would like to tender this document too.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, yes and no. I mean, the answer is -- the witness never asked whether he has ever seen the document before. And also could I know where the document emanates from it? It's not, as I understand it, a document that comes from our collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We received this document from Republika Srpska. Just a moment. What is the exact name? The team for the investigation of war crimes of Republika Srpska. Ms. Korner, I am certain that this document, first of all, must be in the archives of the CSB Banja Luka, and you have that entire archive. And, second, since it went to the public prosecutor's office, must be at the public prosecutor's office of Banja Luka, I can claim with near certainty that -- that it is in your collection.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure Mr. Zecevic can claim it is in our collection, but at the moment there's nothing to show that we have ever laid eyes on this one before, and we have turned over the whole of the CSB collection bar certain documents is in EDS. So I don't want to comment further on that. My real question is whether this witness is the proper witness for this document to go through because, as I understand it, I believe the answer to the question which he hasn't been asked would be he has never seen this document before. And there are other witnesses coming who will deal with the prosecution of offences. I mean, that's the only thing I raise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I can ask the witness if he -- if can he confirm the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Tutus, have you previously seen this document, and can you confirm your information about whether these individuals were really detained as part of this operation?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the decision on detention?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, all these documents and the letter to the public prosecutor's office that was signed by Mr. Zupljanin, as you say?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally have not seen the decision on detention or the letter to the prosecutor's office. But as for the work-plan and the previous agreements, the chief of the centre had that. I was in attendance as well as the head of the crime service, Zivko Bojic. And Zoran Josic, the head of the crime service, was also present and we wanted to clarify this plan. I know there were certain activities that were engaged and some individuals were detained. But I haven't previously seen this decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the sake of the transcript, perhaps this document could be marked for identification now. And then we could see whether Ms. Korner has any comments to make a little later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no objection to that course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 1D199, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document that I would like to show you is 79, tab 79. 1D00-1723 is the number of the document. It's a criminal report dated the 25th of June, 1992, sent to the public prosecutor's office, signed by the chief of the centre, Mr. Stojan Zupljanin. It has to do with criminal proceedings instituted against Branko Palackovic and several other unidentified perpetrators for six crimes against general security. The description says that on a number of occasions in April, they inflicted damage on restaurants and other facilities, and this was done by -- owned by Muslims and Albanians. Mahmut Ganic, Limani Safik, Hidic Refik are mentioned. The citizen Kemal, Duzel Irfan, and so on. Do you remember from the operations plan that one of the items had to do with arresting the group led by Palackovic, Branko. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that Mr. Palackovic was arrested?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I assume that this criminal report and all the documents attached to it are documents you are not familiar with. You haven't seen them?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For this reason I would suggest that this document also be marked for identification. If there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit 1D200, marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you please have a look at document 76, tab 76, 1D00-1503 is the number of the document. This document is a criminal report dated the 23rd of June, 1992. And yet again, it's a criminal report filed against Palackovic, Brane Palackovic and his group that consists of 14 known and over 15 unknown individuals. But in this case, it concerns 37 crimes listed in the -- in the charges on page 3 in the e-court system and in your document. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since you have already previously confirmed that you know that Mr. Brane Palackovic was arrested, as well as his group, I assume that this also concerns this document. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have a look at page 3. You have the handwritten number 03 that has been added, and then it says that on that occasion they physically injured Kobilj, Dzevad. And afterwards, a certain Sinisa Milovic used a pistol with which he killed Mustafa Smailagic, the son of Zaim, born in 1942, in Banja Luka. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In both cases, Muslims were the injured parties; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Item 2, it says Obradovac Midhat was -- had his papers controlled and about 270.000 dinars were confiscated from him. Can you see that under item 2?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, this is Muslim who is the injured party; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Then under item 3, Enis Mahmutovic's papers were checked, after which some of his money was taken, 120.000 dinars, 200 Swiss francs, 50 German marks. His vehicle was confiscated, and he was hit with a rifle, with a rifle-butt. This person is also a Muslim person. He is the injured party. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Items 4 and 5 on the following page, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, and up to 12, up to item 12, all these individuals are Muslims, all these injured parties are Muslims. Zulic Enver, Laha Marija, Kemal Duzel, Sjenica Jelenko, Muharem Sibic, Alija Bojic, son of Hasan.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Jelenko Sjenica, that's the perpetrator.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Duzel, Kemal, yes; Zulic, Enver, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So as not to waste any time, if you have a look at this document, the injured parties are mainly Muslims and Croats but there are also some injured parties who are Serbs. And one crime report covers all of them. One crime report against Brane Palackovic and his group. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since this criminal report was sent from the CSB and it was signed by the chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin, I assume that this document as well as the documents attached to the criminal report are not documents that you have already seen. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen them. But I'm looking for the end of the criminal report.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The end of the report is on page 12.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right, the chief of the centre signed it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would like to request that this document also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D201, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When we had a look at the operative plan, do you remember that reference was made to fires, to planting explosive devices and so on and so forth. Please have a look at tab 89. 1D00-5252 is the number. It's a document dated the 15th of July, 1992, signed by the chief of the centre, and the title is: "An analysis of fires in the Territory of the Municipality of Banja Luka for the first six months of the year 1992."

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D00-5252. We have the English version up on the screen. Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 3 of this document, it says that a total of 43 fires were caused; 17 were intentionally caused; 16 caused by accident; and in the case of ten fires, the reasons for these fires are unknown. Item 4 of this document, the last sentence says that the ethnicity of the owners of damaged facilities -- well, 8 Muslims [Realtime transcript read in error "militaries"], five Croats, one Serb, and three others. That's the ethnicity of the injured parties. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the last page --

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the second page not the third page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. And on the last page of the document, it says the employees of the crime service in the CSB have identified the perpetrators of two cases of arson at the Centar kebab restaurant owned by Safik Limani, and [indiscernible] florist shop owned by Mahmut Ganic, and a criminal report regarding this has been submitted against Brane Palackovic. Can you see this?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On page 81, line 8, when I was referring to the document and to the ethnicity of the owners of certain buildings that were destroyed, I said that there were eight Muslims, five Croats, one Serb, and three others. I see it says "eight militaries" here. This is obviously a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Have you seen this document entitled "Analysis of fires"?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember but it was probably received.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, given that the CSB has certain duties, well, the CSB would forward such reports to all SJBs. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But since you can't remember --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections, I would also suggest that we mark this document for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit 1D202, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To illustrate what we have been discussing, I have in mind, in fact, your claim that, in 1992, the SJB and CSB in Banja Luka processed all crimes regardless of the ethnicity of the victims or the perpetrators. Please have a look at document under tab 61. 1D03-1775 is the number of the document. It's a report on the arrest -- on the arrest of certain individuals. 17th of April, 1992, is the date. Signed by Mr. Stojan Zupljanin, the chief of the centre. He is informing the investigative judge that in accordance with the Law on Criminal Procedure, detention has been ordered for up to three days for Damir Halilovic, son of Bajro because there are grounds to believe that he committed the crime of murder. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the following page, it's page 2 in the e-court system, we have the crime report against Halilovic, Damir, because it is suspected that he committed the crime of murder against Enis Krkic. Enis Krkic, son of Hajro, born on the 3rd of November, 1950, in Banja Luka. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, in this case, the perpetrator in the crime are Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this crime was processed in accordance with the Code on Criminal Procedure?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell me, in the documents I can see that this case was mainly dealt with - it's on page 5 of the document - by an authorised official. It's an Official Note. It was signed by a certain -- it's page 5, if you have a look at the whole document. Page 5. It's an Official Note signed by an authorised official whose name is Adem Alisa?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know this person, Mr. Alisa? He was probably an inspector.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He was an inspector in the crime department.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the 17th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there are no objections.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And I assume that you haven't previously seen this document since it was signed by the chief of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Well, I didn't look at such documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So if there are no objections, I would also like to request that this document be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D203, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please have a look at the document under tab 62 now. 1D00-5478 is the number of the document. It's a crime report. On page 2 you will see that this report was filed by the Banja Luka SJB. Your chief of the department, Zoran Josic, signed it. Have a look at the following page. It was provided to the public prosecutor's office in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D5478. 5478. Or is it 5978; I do apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a criminal report against Jasmin Hajric.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry, 5978. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you see this criminal report?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The criminal report says that he's a recidivist, a person who had been recorded at the public security station before as bent on crime.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it says so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in the form of the criminal report, he says -- it says he is a fugitive.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You see his personal details. It says where he served in the army, Bileca and Bitolj, rank sergeant, and then he says, Currently at large.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Jasmin Hajic is without doubt a Muslim, as the criminal report indicates?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And it's filed against him for the crime of robbery against Niko Cosic, aged 73. From the pocket of this man's shirt, Jasmin Hajric took a sum of money. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Niko Cosic could be a Croat, judging by the last name?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is certainly a Croat.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since this is a document of the public security station Banja Luka, signed by your chief of section, chief of department, Zoran Josic --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I hope there is no objection to the admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D204, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now please turn to tab 63. The document is 1D00-5968, dated 18 May 1992. It's a record of on-site investigation sent to the public prosecutor's office with the Official Note attached, signed by department chief, Zoran Josic. Can you see the document?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a case where the injured party is Zlatko Milovac. I suppose a Serb.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The incident happened at 1.00 a.m. in Banja Luka when unidentified perpetrators using automatic fire-arms caused damage to a private business called Ring in Banja Luka. You see that?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You will see on the last page of the document is the Official Note made by an authorised officer on the 14th of April, April 1992, from a certain Teufik Dzambegovic - I believe a Muslim - who was a security guard in this catering establishment that was targeted, and he who was on the scene.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So in this case, the injured party is either a Serb or a Croat, and the unidentified perpetrators were in camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If there is no objection, since this is a document of your public security station, I would like to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D205, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry. The next tab is 68. 1D00-6660. Sorry. Let's move to 70. 1D00-1291. I apologise for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Again, it's a report on arrest and conveyance, dated 18 June 1992. The signature is that of chief of the centre, Stojan Zupljanin, submitted to the security services centre in Banja Luka. And it's a report and the arrest and conveyance of a certain Dragoslav Kuzmic, father's name Milorad, mother's name Savka. Obviously a Serb; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And is he suspected as an accomplice in the crime of murder perpetrated by four unidentified persons, three of them in camouflage uniform, when Mustafa Smailagic, son of Zaim, was shot dead with two bullets. You remember in the operative work-plan one of the items was to establish the identity of perpetrators of the murder of this person Smailagic Mustafa?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mustafa Smailagic is obviously indisputably a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And this document, the criminal report is dated 18 June 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Since this document, the criminal report and the attached documentation emanate from the chief of the centre, I don't suppose you have seen it before.

utterances.speaker: VLADIMIR TUTUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suggest that this document be MFI'd, if there is no objection from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit 1D206, marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now I should kindly to ask you to open tab 72.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you probably couldn't complete another line of questions before the time for the adjournment in less than a minute, so ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honours. I was trying to be as -- as -- as -- as possible to use as much time as I can. But I understand and I follow. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- so we take the adjournment and we reconvene, if memory serves, in Courtroom III, at 2.15 tomorrow afternoon. Mr. Tutus, I remind you of what I would have said earlier about not communicating with anyone during the adjournment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of March, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
